title: 第一卷 第4章 克扣工钱
novel_title: 津门武圣，从苦力开始每日结算
content_zh:
雨后的码头，泥水没过脚踝。

    空气中弥漫着腐烂的鱼腥味和煤渣味。

    陆川站在煤堆旁，手里拿着一把铁铲。

    他在铲煤。

    动作机械，一下又一下。

    昨天的盗窃案在码头闹得沸沸扬扬。

    巡捕房的人来转了一圈，带走了守门的老头，问了几句，又放了。

    理由是证据不足。

    赵扒皮站在棚子底下，脸色黑得像锅底。

    那座洋钟没找回来，他赔了巡捕房一笔封口费，心疼得直抽抽。

    最后，这笔账算在了守门老头头上。

    扣了三个月工钱，算是惩罚。

    至于那个真正的“贼”，赵扒皮没证据，只能忍着。

    但他那双三角眼，时不时就往煤堆这边瞟。

    眼神阴毒，像条盯着猎物的毒蛇。

    陆川视若无睹。

    他现在的注意力，都在肚子里。

    饿！

    那种仿佛能把胃壁消化掉的饥饿感，又来了。

    昨晚突破【铜皮】，消耗太大。

    两个馒头，根本不够塞牙缝。

    “发工钱了！”

    一声吆喝，打破了码头的死寂。

    工友们放下手里的活，一个个翘首以盼地围了过来。

    赵扒皮手里拿着个账本，身后跟着两个打手。

    “张三，九个铜板。”

    “李四，八个铜板。”

    一个个名字报下来，铜板和大洋叮当响。

    很快，轮到了陆川。

    “陆川。”

    赵扒皮合上账本，从兜里摸出几枚铜板，数了数。

    “五个铜板。”

    陆川接过钱，没说话。

    但他眉头皱了一下。

    “赵爷，算错了吧？”

    旁边一个老工友忍不住插嘴，“昨天那是卸船的重活，说好的是十二个铜板。”

    赵扒皮眼皮一抬，斜睨了那老工友一眼。

    “十二个？”

    “你们这帮子臭苦力，没有老子你们早饿死了！”

    “收你们点平安捐就不乐意了？”

    “老子难道不吃饭吗？”

    “一天天的，都掉钱眼里了！”

    赵扒皮指着老工友破口大骂。

    老工友也不敢还嘴，只是握紧手中的铜板，讷讷地往后退了两步。

    赵扒皮冷笑一声，再次指着陆川的鼻子喝骂道，“还有你，昨天那是干活吗？那在是偷懒！”

    “五百斤的煤，居然铲了半个时辰才完事。”

    “差点耽误了船期，老子扣你点钱怎么了？”

    谁不知道昨天那是赵扒皮故意整人，但没人敢站出来说句公道话。

    就像赵扒皮说的一样，他还真就是这帮苦力的衣食父母。

    陆川看着手里的五个铜板，又看了看赵扒皮。

    “行。”

    陆川把钱揣进兜里，转身就走。

    赵扒皮愣了一下，他以为陆川会闹。

    这混蛋玩意，前几天看自己的眼神十分的不舒服。

    为防止陆川闹事，赵扒皮特意找了两个打手。

    就等着给陆川一点教训。

    没想到，这就怂了？

    “切，穷鬼命。”

    赵扒皮啐了一口骂道，“给脸不要脸的东西。”

    ......

    日头偏西。

    码头上的人少了一半。

    陆川正准备收拾东西回家，忽然听到一阵骚乱。

    “赵爷，赵爷您高抬贵手！”

    “小女还小，不懂事，冲撞了您，我给您赔罪！”

    声音是从赵扒皮的棚子那边传来的。

    带着哭腔，还有膝盖磕在地上的闷响。
content_en:
At the pier after the rain, the muddy water reached the ankles.

    The air smelled of rotting fish and cinders.

    Lu Chuan stood next to the coal pile, holding a shovel in his hand.

    He was shoveling coal.

    The action is mechanical, one after another.

    Yesterday's theft caused quite a stir at the docks.

    The people from the patrol room came and walked around, took away the old man guarding the door, asked a few questions, and then let him go.

    The reason is insufficient evidence.

    Zhao Bapi stood under the shed, his face as dark as the bottom of a pot.

    The foreign clock was not recovered, so he paid the police station a sum of money for keeping it secret, and he felt heartbroken.

    In the end, the account was settled on the old gatekeeper.

    Three months' wages were deducted as punishment.

    As for the real "thief", Zhao Bapi had no evidence and could only endure it.

    But his triangular eyes would glance towards the coal pile from time to time.

    His eyes were sinister, like a poisonous snake staring at its prey.

    Lu Chuan turned a blind eye.

    His focus now is on his stomach.

    Hungry!

    The hunger that seemed to be able to digest the stomach wall came again.

    I broke through [Copper Skin] last night and it consumed too much.

    Two steamed buns are not enough to fill the gap between teeth.

    "The wages are paid!"

    A shout broke the dead silence of the dock.

    The workers put down their work and gathered around eagerly.

    Zhao Papi held a ledger in his hand, followed by two thugs.

    "Zhang San, nine copper coins."

    "John Doe, eight copper coins."

    The names were announced one by one, and the copper plates jingled against the ocean.

    Soon, it was Lu Chuan's turn.

    "Lu Chuan."

    Zhao Papi closed the account book, took out a few copper plates from his pocket, and counted them.

    "Five coppers."

    Lu Chuan took the money and said nothing.

    But he frowned.

    "Master Zhao, is your calculation wrong?"

    An old worker next to him couldn't help but interject, "Yesterday it was a heavy job of unloading the ship, and the price was agreed to be twelve copper coins."

    Zhao Papi raised his eyelids and glanced sideways at the old worker.

    "Twelve?"

    "You bunch of stinky coolies, if it weren't for me you would have starved to death!"

    "Aren't you happy to accept some peace donations from you?"

    "Don't I want to eat?"

    "Every day, I am losing money!"

    Zhao Bapi pointed at the old worker and cursed.

    The old co-worker didn't dare to talk back, he just clenched the copper plate in his hand and took two steps back.

    Zhao Papi sneered, pointed at Lu Chuan's nose again and cursed, "And you, was that work yesterday? That was laziness!"

    "It took half an hour to shovel five hundred kilograms of coal."

    "I almost delayed the shipping date. Why did I deduct some money from you?"

    Who doesn't know that Zhao Bapi deliberately harassed people yesterday, but no one dared to stand up and say something fair.

    Just like Zhao Bapi said, he is really the food and clothing parent of these coolies.

    Lu Chuan looked at the five copper coins in his hand, and then at Zhao Papi.

    "Okay."

    Lu Chuan put the money in his pocket, turned around and left.

    Zhao Bapi was stunned for a moment, thinking that Lu Chuan would make trouble.

    This bastard, the way he looked at me a few days ago was very uncomfortable.

    In order to prevent Lu Chuan from causing trouble, Zhao Papi specially found two thugs.

    Just waiting to teach Lu Chuan a lesson.

    Unexpectedly, this is so timid?

    "Tsk, poor man's life."

    Zhao Papi spat and cursed, "Give me something shameless."

    ...

    The sun is to the west.

    There were half as many people on the dock.

    Lu Chuan was about to pack his things and go home when he suddenly heard a commotion.

    "Master Zhao, Master Zhao, you are so noble!"

    "My little girl is still young and ignorant. I bumped into you. I will apologize to you!"

    The sound came from Zhao Papi's shed.

    With a cry and a muffled sound of his knees hitting the ground.
